newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL interbank rates stay firm on short-end squeeze.
newsitem.headline: KL interbank rates stay firm on short-end squeeze.

text.p: Interbank rates continued to rise on Wednesday due to a shortage of funds at the short-end of the market, dealers said.
The higher rates also reflected a rise in the overnight interbank rate to 9.0 percent on Tuesday, they said.
"The market is still tight and rates will remain high until we see new inflows," said a dealer with a Malaysian bank.
"In the meantime, those who borrow short are suffering," he said.
Dealers said the tightness was caused by a mismatch of funds, with foreign banks holding a lot of funds while local banks were short.
One-week money was traded at 8.80 percent, two-week at 8.90 percent and three-week at 8.70 percent. They were at 8.0/8.50 percent on Tuesday.
The one-month rate was at 8.30 percent against 8.0/8.20, while three-month money was steady at 8.0/8.10 percent.
The overnight rate was expected to remain between 8.5 and 9.0 percent, dealers said.
Interest rate futures on the Malaysia Monetary Exchange remained soft on the back of a firmer cash market.
At 0300 GMT, the three-month Kuala Lumpur Interbank Offered Rate (KLIBOR) June contract was down four points to 92.30, or an implied yield of 7.70 percent.
September contract fell three to 92.48, or 7.52 percent and December was down two to 92.56, or 7.44.
